clue.text: Do they advertise drama by W Shakespeare?

definitions.text: Do they advertise drama by W Shakespeare?

parts.note: a drama is a play
W Shakespeare is William, or Bill, so the letters BILL S stand for his name

explanation.surface: A question about posters promoting a staging of a Shakespeare piece.
explanation.walkthrough: W Shakespeare is written as BILL S, using the short form of William; 'by' just joins the pieces, and the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre posters announcing a production are the very things that advertise a show such as one of Shakespeare's.

indicators.note: shortly says the word for piece is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a piece is a part
to snip is to cut

explanation.surface: A cook's instruction to cut a vegetable into small bits.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsnip is a pale root vegetable, an example of the class named.

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters of annoyed are thrashing about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone irritated and in difficulty is looking for a painkiller.
explanation.definitionFit: An anodyne is a painkilling medicine, so it is a source of relief from pain.

clue.text: Refuse to touch poster for criminal

parts.note: to black goods is a trade-union term for boycotting them, refusing to handle them
a poster is one who posts, a mailer

explanation.surface: Someone declines to handle a placard that was put up for a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poster' looks like a placard, but here it means someone who posts letters; to 'black' work is the British union practice of boycotting it.
explanation.definitionFit: An extortioner who demands money with threats is a type of criminal.

clue.text: Diplomat inattentive at the end: he's left something

parts.note: a legate is an envoy or papal diplomat

indicators.note: at the end picks out only the closing letter of the word inattentive

explanation.surface: A diplomat who drifted off at the close of proceedings has departed, leaving something behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like departed, but the definition means someone to whom something has been left in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A beneficiary named in a will is one to whom something has been bequeathed.

parts.note: so means very, as in so kind
other means different

explanation.surface: A baby product described as quite unlike the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy or pacifier given to calm an infant is an item for a baby.

clue.text: Prepares for holiday: two join the scrum

definitions.meaning: puts clothes into a suitcase before going away
in rugby a scrum is formed by the two teams' forwards, each group of eight known as a pack

explanation.surface: A rugby player gets the suitcase ready while two teammates go into the scrum.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the forwards of each side bind together as a unit; a scrum is the two such units pushing against each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Filling a suitcase readies one for a trip, and rugby forwards in a group form the units that meet in a scrum.

indicators.note: not to finish says the word for choose loses its last letter

parts.note: to pick is to choose

explanation.surface: Someone is still deciding, unwilling to complete the choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb, but it is a noun: a still photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a single photograph, and a pic is informal for a photograph.

clue.text: Palace attendant has no time for messenger

indicators.note: has no says a letter is taken out of the attendant's title

parts.note: a courtier attends at a royal court or palace

explanation.surface: A royal attendant too busy to deliver a message himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who carries packages or messages for a living is a messenger.

clue.text: Detailed plan to bring deer up to little spot

parts.note: a spec, short for specification, is a detailed plan

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for deer is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an elk is a large deer

explanation.surface: A plan for bringing a deer to a small location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spot' looks like a place to bring the deer, but it is the definition; in a down clue 'up' means the deer is read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A speckle is a small mark or fleck, a tiny spot of colour.

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the German yes after the port, written to its right

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
Dieter is a German name, and ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: A slimmer approves of fortified wine from Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dieter' looks like a slimmer but is a German man; 'port wine' looks like one phrase, but port is the Brazilian city and 'on' puts the German yes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine from northern Spain, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Valid reason to contribute to this

definitions.meaning: a sound justification for doing something
a charity or worthy aim is something one donates to

explanation.definitionFit: A worthy charity is something given to, and a sound justification is a fair cause for action.

indicators.note: heard says the entry is spoken alike with the horse's cry

parts.note: a horse's cry is a neigh

explanation.surface: A horse whinnies a refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nay is an old or formal word for a negative reply.

clue.text: One may pull the plug on this sort of drama

definitions.text: One may pull the plug on this
definitions.meaning: a basin in a kitchen is emptied by pulling out its stopper
a British genre of gritty realist plays and films about working-class home life

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull the plug' looks like cancelling a show, but it is the literal plug of a basin.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchen-sink drama is the 1950s-60s British realist genre, and a sink is where a plug gets pulled.

parts.note: to net is to secure or catch
curtains is slang for death or the end

explanation.surface: Executions guarantee death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hangings' looks like executions but means window drapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lightweight sheer drapes over a window are fabric that hangs, so they are hangings.

definitions.meaning: a bishop or other senior cleric
split as ..., before being late, which is what being on time means

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: split the entry as PRE (before) and LATE, so it reads as 'before late'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop or archbishop is a senior cleric, a high-ranking churchman.

clue.text: One's finished working on Hebridean island

parts.note: re means on or concerning
Tiree is an island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone has stopped work on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiree is one of the Inner Hebrides, the islands off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A pensioner who has stopped employment is one whose working life is over.

indicators.note: the letters of Oswald's are formulated again, unluckily jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A rule attributed to someone named Oswald about things going wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Sod's law is the British name for the maxim that if something can go wrong, it will.
explanation.definitionFit: This saying that misfortune strikes whenever it can is a pessimistic rule about bad luck.

clue.text: Squalid area, where you can't keep your feet?

definitions.meaning: a run-down urban district of vagrants

definitions.text: where you can't keep your feet?
definitions.meaning: read as a row of houses where you skid and slip over

explanation.definitionFit: A rundown neighbourhood of the destitute is a squalid district, and skidding is losing one's footing.

parts.note: to rave is to talk wildly as if mad

explanation.surface: A dishonest deputy loses his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb, to make wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprave someone is to make them morally bad, to pervert them.

parts.note: ailing means falling ill

explanation.surface: A wife falling ill and moaning about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wailing is crying out in grief or protest, a loud form of lamenting.

clue.text: Runner losing pounds becomes more complacent

indicators.note: losing says a letter is taken out of the runner's title

parts.note: a runner is one who smuggles goods, as in gun-runner
L is the abbreviation for pounds, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: An athlete who sheds weight grows self-satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' looks like an athlete and 'losing pounds' like dieting, but the runner is a smuggler of contraband.
explanation.definitionFit: Being smug is being self-satisfied, so the comparative means more self-satisfied.

clue.text: Put away, he hates to reform

indicators.note: to reform means the letters of he hates are re-formed into a new order

explanation.surface: He hates being put away to be reformed, like a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe a sword is to put it away in its scabbard.

definitions.meaning: silencing someone, as by covering the mouth
a gag is a joke, so a comedian making them is at this

explanation.definitionFit: Muzzling someone stops them speaking, and gags are a comedian's jokes.

indicators.note: not entirely says only part of the phrase bright one is used, its outer letters dropped

explanation.surface: A personal computer that is not wholly clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PC' looks like a computer or a police constable, but here it is 'politically correct'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fashionably liberal in one's views is the informal sense matching politically correct.

clue.text: Fresh mint I repent getting chopped up

indicators.note: chopped up says the letters of mint I repent are cut up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A cook regrets that fresh mint is being minced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' looks like a description of the mint, but it means cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh in the sense of cheeky or forward means rude to one's elders.

indicators.note: short says the musical's title is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: Gigi is a stage and film musical

explanation.surface: A brief musical show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short musical' looks like a description of the show; it is the musical Gigi with its last letter removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A gig is a live engagement by a band or comedian, a single show.

clue.text: Keep on editing paper? Not I

indicators.note: editing says the letters of paper, not and I are reworked into another order

explanation.surface: An editor is asked whether to continue working on the newspaper, with someone refusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not I' looks like a refusal but supplies letters for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep someone on in a post is to name them to it again.

parts.note: PA is per annum, Latin for every year
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A question about annual income.
explanation.definitionFit: Wages or salary received for work are one's earnings.

indicators.note: holding says the word for spot keeps the letter for one inside it

parts.note: a dot is a spot
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone calls himself a fool for spotting something while holding it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupid person, a dimwit, is a fool.

clue.text: Went back to play with feeble physique

parts.note: went, as in went to the toilet, is weed, urinated

indicators.note: back to picks the rear letter of the word play

explanation.surface: Someone frail returned to take part in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went back' looks like a phrase meaning returned; 'Went' is a coy way of saying urinated (WEED), and 'back to play' gives the final letter of play.
explanation.definitionFit: Weedy is an informal word for thin and weak, so it describes a puny body.

indicators.note: broken says the letters of gang reuse are smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A gang reuses a broken oiling tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand pump for forcing grease into machinery bearings is a tool for lubricating.
